say: You give it a diagram with triangles and a parallelogram that share a base and a height. It finds the unknown **area**, and cites Theorem 16.
Theorem 16: the area of a triangle is half of $\text{base} \times \text{height}$, and it is the same whichever side you take as the base.
what.in: triangle or parallelogram, with area given

how.ordinary: Ordinary level used it once, on Paper 2 in 2015: a 5-mark part finding the areas of triangles inside a parallelogram.

example.question:
$PQRS$ is a parallelogram with area $360\ \text{m}^2$. $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$.
(i) Find the area of the triangle $PQS$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

steps.title: Triangle on the same base
steps.say: Triangle $PQS$ has the same base $[PS]$ and the same height as the parallelogram. By Theorem 16 it is **half** the parallelogram.

steps.title: Triangle on side QR
steps.say: Take $[QR]$ as the base. Triangle $PQR$ has the same base and height as the parallelogram, so its area is half again.

steps.title: Halve the base
steps.say: $T$ is the midpoint, so $|QT| = \tfrac{1}{2}|QR|$. The height from $P$ is the same, so triangle $PQT$ has **half** the area of $PQR$.

lines.text: Same height, half the base: half the area.

say: You give it a circle with a tangent. It finds an unknown **length** or angle, and cites Theorem 20.
Theorem 20: a tangent is **perpendicular** to the radius at the point of contact. That gives you a right angle, so Pythagoras and trigonometry work.

how.higher: Higher level used it in six parts on Paper 2 between 2015 and 2020, three of them with Theorem 20 as the main skill: the right angle at the point of contact is the first step of a longer part, worth 10 to 15 marks.

example.question:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $5$ cm. $[PT]$ is a tangent to the circle at $T$, and $|OP| = 13$ cm.
(i) Find $|PT|$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $OTP$.

steps.title: Mark the right angle
steps.say: $[OT]$ is a radius and $[PT]$ is a tangent at $T$. By Theorem 20 they are perpendicular, so $|\angle OTP| = 90^\circ$.

lines.text: Triangle $OTP$ is right-angled at $T$. $[OP]$ is the hypotenuse.

steps.title: Use Pythagoras
steps.say: Write Pythagoras with the numbers in, then solve for $|PT|$.

steps.title: Find the area
steps.say: The two shorter sides are perpendicular, so use them as base and height.

say: You give it a parallelogram with a diagonal drawn. It finds an unknown **angle** or side, and cites Corollary 1.
Corollary 1: a diagonal splits a parallelogram into **two congruent triangles**, so the matching angles and sides are equal.

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|\angle ABC| = (4x + 10)^\circ$ and $|\angle CDA| = (6x - 20)^\circ$. Find $x$ and $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.title: Draw the diagonal
steps.say: Draw the diagonal $[AC]$. By Corollary 1, triangles $ABC$ and $CDA$ are congruent.

lines.text: $B$ in the first triangle matches $D$ in the second.

steps.title: Matching angles are equal
steps.say: In congruent triangles the matching angles are equal. $|\angle ABC|$ matches $|\angle CDA|$, so set them equal.

steps.title: Solve for x
steps.say: Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.

say: You give it three parallel lines cutting one transversal into **equal** pieces. It finds the pieces on a second transversal, and cites Theorem 11.
Theorem 11: if the pieces are equal on one transversal, they are equal on **every** transversal.
what.in: three parallel lines, equal on one transversal

how.higher: Higher level has used it twice on Paper 2: in 2015 as the proof of the theorem itself (20 marks in Question 6), and in 2018 as the step inside the proof of the ratio theorem (a 15-mark part).

example.question: The parallel lines $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ cut the transversal $[AC]$ with $|AB| = |BC|$. They cut the second transversal $[DF]$ at $D$, $E$ and $F$. $|DE| = (2x + 1)$ cm and $|EF| = (4x - 9)$ cm. Find $x$ and $|DF|$.

steps.title: State the theorem
steps.say: Three parallel lines cut equal pieces $|AB| = |BC|$ on one transversal. By Theorem 11 they cut equal pieces on every transversal.

steps.title: Make the equation
steps.say: Put the two lengths equal to each other.

steps.title: Solve for x
steps.say: Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.

steps.title: Find the whole length
steps.say: Find $|DE|$, then double it, since $|EF|$ is the same.
